titulo_es: Distinguir ogni, qualche, troppo and tutto

texto: **Ogni** and **qualche** only admit names in **singular**: **ogni studente** (each student); **qualche giorno** (one day / a few days). Never say * qualche giorni *.
**Troppo/a/i/e** denotes excess and agrees in gender and number: **troppo traffico** (too much traffic); **troppe persone** (too many people).
**Tutto** requires defined article before defined substantive: **tutto il giorno** (all day); **tutta la notte** (all night); **tutti gli studenti** (all students).

filas: Variable in gender and number + article

frases.it: C'era molta gente al mercato questa mattina?
frases.es: ¿Había mucha gente en el mercado esta mañana?
frases.en: Was there a lot of people on the market this morning?
analisis: There were a lot of people.

frases.it: Sì, c'erano troppe persone e faceva caldissimo!
frases.es: Sí, ¡había demasiadas personas y hacía muchísimo calor!
frases.en: Yeah, there were too many people and it was so hot!

frases.it: E sei riuscito a comprare quello che cercavi?
frases.en: And you got to buy what you were looking for?

frases.it: Solo qualche mela e il pane: ogni banco aveva una fila lunghissima.
frases.es: Solo unas manzanas y el pan: cada puesto tenía una cola larguísima.
frases.en: Only a few apples and bread: each place had a very long tail.

frases.it: Capisco! Allora riposati per tutto il pomeriggio.
frases.es: ¡Entiendo! Entonces descansa durante toda la tarde.
frases.en: I understand! Then rest all afternoon.

intro: It perfects the use of indefinite quantifiers such as troppo, tutto, ogni and qualche according to its syntactic rules.
